title: The Five-Step Conversion (Master Method)
description: The master conversion — the framework’s core procedure — in full: STEP 1 — NAME the pattern in plain words (no jargon, no verdict); STEP 2 — DIAGRAM nodes and arrows (what feeds what — draw it); STEP 3 — FIND the key node (where do the dynamics hinge?); STEP 4 — FORMALIZE minimally (attractor? loop? oscillator? — just enough); STEP 5 — SPECIFY reuse (name the software, story, or AI design where this works). Each step’s FALSIFIER: vague naming, missing arrows, no hinge found, over-formalizing, unspecified reuse — fail any and redo. The method’s output: a mapping card ready for the databases. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only — not medical advice.

title: Pattern Naming: The Plain-Words Rule
description: The naming — step 1 deepened — enforces PLAIN WORDS FIRST: describe the pattern as you’d explain it to a smart twelve-year-old — "the worry that won’t get tested," "the stuck that feeds itself." FORBIDDEN in step 1: clinical terms, Latin, verdicts ("disorder," "broken," "toxic"). The rule’s reason: jargon smuggles conclusions; plain words expose structure. TEST: if the name contains a judgment, rename. The name is the foundation — everything diagrams from it. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Diagramming: Nodes and Arrows

TOOLS: whiteboard, paper, or any graph tool — the medium doesn’t matter, the arrows do. A diagram with unlabeled arrows is a doodle — label everything. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. title: Key-Node Hunting
description: The hunt — step 3 deepened — asks THREE QUESTIONS: (1) If I could change ONE thing, what changes everything? (2) Where does the system PREVENT its own correction? (3) What would a designer REMOVE to break this? Techniques: PERTURBATION THOUGHT-EXPERIMENTS (mentally wiggle each node), the FIVE-WHYS (drill to the hinge), and INVERSION (ask what would make it worse — the answer reveals the node). OUTPUT: one named node with a one-sentence mechanism. If you find three key nodes, you haven’t dug deep enough — keep hunting. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Minimal Formalization: Just Enough Math
description: The formalization — step 4 deepened — obeys JUST-ENOUGH: use the SMALLEST formalism that captures the dynamics — usually one of the five primitives (attractor, loop, oscillator, prediction engine, salience map) plus the key node named. FORBIDDEN: stochastic differential equations where a diagram suffices; custom primitives where composition works; precision theater (three decimals on guessed parameters). TEST: can a colleague rebuild the diagram from your formalism alone? If yes, enough. If it needs a textbook, too much. Formalism serves reuse — nothing more. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: The Wall Check (Ethics Method)
description: The check — the ethics gate — runs on EVERY mapping before publication: (1) PERSONS? — does it describe, imply, or approach any real person or group? If yes: STOP. (2) CLAIMS? — does any sentence read as medical fact, advice, or promise? If yes: REWRITE. (3) DISCLAIMER? — is the full text present on the record? If no: ADD. (4) LANGUAGE? — person-first, non-stigmatizing throughout? If no: FIX. (5) REFERRAL? — are professionals and 988 mentioned? If no: ADD. Five gates, all must pass — the check takes ten minutes and prevents every category of harm the framework anticipates. A Signature ethics method by Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Composition Mapping (Interop Method)
description: The interop — the composition method — maps FAMILY COMBINATIONS: take two mapped patterns, OVERLAY their diagrams (shared nodes? conflicting arrows?), NAME the composition (loop × attractor = "bailing in the well"), and SPECIFY the composed key node (which hinge dominates?). The method’s value: real systems are compositions — single-family mappings are training wheels. OUTPUT: an interop card for the master table. RULE: compose only mapped families — never improvise unmapped ones into compositions. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Validation: Does the Mapping Work?
description: The validation — the honesty — tests mappings three ways: STRUCTURAL (do practitioners recognize the dynamics? — the "yes, that’s my system" test), PREDICTIVE (does the key node predict where interventions land? — the design bet), and GENERATIVE (does the mapping produce non-obvious reuses? — the creativity dividend). A mapping passing all three is KEEP; passing two is REVISE; passing one is CUT. The validation’s boundary: it tests DESIGN UTILITY — never clinical validity, which the framework neither claims nor tests. Honest about what "works" means. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: The Audit Method (Engagement Ethics)
description: The audit — the applied — scores product loops: TOLERANCE DRIFT present? CUE DENSITY engineered? VARIABLE SCHEDULES deployed? EXIT COSTS imposed? VULNERABILITY TARGETED? The method’s teeth: audits are PUBLISHED (sunlight), REPEATED (quarterly — drift creeps), and INDEPENDENT (auditors don’t report to growth teams). An audit method with no independence is theater — the method specifies governance, not just scoring. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: The Premise-First Facilitation
description: The facilitation — the premise-first — runs DIVERGENT meetings: OPEN with prior surfacing (each side states assumptions — written, visible), BUILD the shared instrument (what measurement would convince both?), RUN it if possible (or schedule the run), and CLOSE with updated priors (what changed? — logged). The method’s magic: most "disagreements" dissolve at step 1 (different premises, both valid) or step 2 (the instrument settles it) — conclusion-debate, the futile kind, rarely needed. For strategy, science, and community conflicts. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: The Oath-Taking Ceremony (Method)
description: The ceremony — the oath-taking — makes ethics MEMORABLE: practitioners gather, each states their domain (products, AI, stories), the oath is read aloud in its family edition, each speaks the closing line ("I build for the user’s arrival..."), and the signed oaths are POSTED (team wall, repo README, course site). The method’s psychology: public commitment outperforms private intention — and posted oaths invite accountability. Corny? Deliberately — solemnity is a technology for remembering. The ceremony closes every course, every audit engagement, every team onboarding into framework work. A Signature method by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.
